\section{Full Experimental Grids}
\label{app:grids}

% Every table here is generated by `python -m experiments.make_report` from the committed run
% JSONs. The main text carries one paragraph and one headline number per finding; this appendix
% carries the grid behind each. Because both come from the same script, trimming Section 4 for
% length cannot separate a claim from the numbers that support it.

Every table in this appendix is generated from the committed run JSONs by
\texttt{experiments/make\_report.py}; none of it is typed by hand. Cells are means over the
stated number of seeds with the sample standard deviation, and a cell that finished above 95\,\%
of the unigram baseline is counted as collapsed rather than averaged into a mean, because a mean
over a mixture of runs that learned and runs that did not measures neither.

\subsection{The switch ladder}
\label{app:grid-switches}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering\footnotesize
\input{figures/table_switches}
\caption{Each of the ten differences priced twice: S1 is the transformer with that one property
replaced by the causal PT's, S2 is the all-PT rung with that one property restored to the
transformer's. $\Delta$ is the distance from the anchor of its own family, signed so that in
\emph{both} families a positive value means the causal PT's version of that property is worse
by that much: in S1 it is what adopting the PT's version costs a transformer, in S2 what
restoring the transformer's version buys the PT. Each rung is the best of four learning rates,
and the S2 anchor moves as the sweep fills in, so the two columns should be read against the
anchors printed above them rather than against each other.}
\label{tab:switches}
\end{table}

\subsection{The global variables}
\label{app:grid-globalhead}

% Eight columns and, once the grid finishes, fifty-four rows: this one spans both columns.
\begin{table*}[h]
\centering\footnotesize
\input{figures/table_globalhead}
\caption{The Appendix B.3.3 global head across initialisation scale, $L_2$ treatment,
distribution and feature count, three seeds, in the configuration the width experiment selected.
$H(Q_g)/\max$ is the entropy of the head posterior as a fraction of its maximum: at $1.000$ the
posterior is uniform and the head's message is a constant label prior rather than the
feed-forward-like operator it is proposed as --- a distinction perplexity alone cannot see. Two
kinds of cell carry no mean. \textit{$n/m$ collapsed} means $n$ of $m$ seeds finished on the
unigram. An italic \textit{range} means no seed reached the unigram but the largest is at least
$1.5\times$ the smallest, so the seeds are not samples of one distribution and their mean would
describe a uniformly mediocre configuration rather than one seed working and two not; every
clean cell in this grid has a ratio below $1.11$ and every reported range above $2.8$.}
\label{tab:globalhead}
\end{table*}
